analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (load-flow diagram at ~272-273 and the reclaimer paragraph at 312-319) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new paragraph at ~1048-1063). No executable code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization or key-handling change is visible. The documented behavior covers retaining free 64 MiB KV segments in a per-pool parking lot outside the grant and ledger charge, and zero-fill-on-demand host pages for new segments. It also covers release of retained segments before eviction or refusal, a proactive allocator-cache sweep, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0 opt-outs.

Security relevance is limited to T-028 (residual KV data in GPU memory), TB-007 (inference engine) and T-041 (prefix cache). Parked segments hold KV backing from released rows, outside the ledger charge and for up to 30 s of idleness. If the implementation reinstalls parked segments without zeroing them, cross-request residue could reach another request in the same process. This would be a same-process, same-provider concern, and the provider operator is already adversarial and can read plaintext in memory (T-011, T-014). The docs state that the next admission reinstalls parked segments but do not say whether contents are cleared or overwritten before reuse. Reuse across requests is also already the baseline in T-028. Because the implementation files (EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, PagedKVGroup.swift, KVPoolReclaimer) are not supplied, I cannot verify zeroing or how the unaccounted parked memory interacts with the memory-cap invariants. The parked backing sits outside the ledger charge and could weaken the cap and availability invariants, but this is unverified. I record this as an integration question rather than a finding. Recommend that the threat-model T-028 text be updated if the code is confirmed to retain unzeroed KV backing across requests. No finding is raised because the evidence is documentation prose only.
